correctness.rationale: Under the explicitly stated finite-dimensional S>0 and K≠0 assumptions the lower K-frame inequality is equivalent to A K K*= A KK* ≤ S. Congruence with S^(-1/2) yields Aopt = ||S^(-1/2)K||^(-2). The published lower estimate λmin(S)/||K||² is valid, but equality in both spectral inequalities requires a common vector from eigenspaces E_{λmin(S)}(S) and E_{||K||²}(KK*). On H=C², K=diag(2,1), Φ=(2e1,e2), S=KK*=diag(4,1), exact energies coincide, so Aopt=1, while λmin(S)/||K||²=1/4. Full author-uploaded 2018 article Prop2.3(i) actually calls 1/4 optimal for this class but its proof establishes only a lower inequality. All inequalities and equality cases are exact.
residual_risks: The generalized-inverse/singular S case is deliberately not asserted.

originality.rationale: The abstract optimal K-frame constant from operator order and Douglas factorization is standard and is not claimed as independent novelty. The specific false 2018 Proposition 2.3(i) and its exact extremal-eigenspace equality criterion, demonstrated by a 2D Parseval K-frame, are a source-specific correction not found in the comparisons. The later 2018/2020 general canonical K-dual results do not automatically state the correction of this eigenvalue quotient; unknown or unindexed errata remain possible.
